column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Hadith 38: “Whoever shows enmity to an ally of Mine”

column2: From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah the Exalted said: Whoever shows enmity to an ally (walī) of Mine, I have declared war on him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him.

And My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks My refuge, I will surely grant him refuge.” Al-Bukhārī reported it.

Al-Bukhārī alone, of all the authors of the books, recorded this hadith. He recorded it from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Karāmah: Khālid ibn Makhlad told us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl told us, Sharīk ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Namir told me,

from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ; and he mentioned the hadith in full, adding at its end: “I have not hesitated over anything I do as I hesitate over the soul of the believer: he dislikes death, and I dislike to cause him grief.”

It is one of the unusual (gharīb) hadiths of the Ṣaḥīḥ. Ibn Karāmah alone narrated it from Khālid, and it is not in the Musnad of Aḥmad; moreover Khālid ibn Makhlad al-Qaṭawānī was criticised by Aḥmad and others,

who said that he has munkar (objectionable) narrations. As for the ʿAṭāʾ in its chain, some say he is Ibn Abī Rabāḥ and others say he is Ibn Yasār, and that he appears named that way in some copies of the Ṣaḥīḥ.
This hadith has also been narrated by other routes, none of which is free of criticism. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Maymūn Abū Ḥamzah, the freed slave of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, narrated it from ʿUrwah,

from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Whoever harms an ally of Mine has made it lawful to wage war on Me. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything like the performance of My obligations,

and My servant draws near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I am his eye with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, his foot with which he walks, his heart with which he understands

and his tongue with which he speaks. If he calls on Me, I answer him; and if he asks of Me, I give to him. I have not hesitated over anything I do as I hesitate over his death; that is because he dislikes death, and I dislike to cause him grief.”
Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and others recorded it, and Imam Aḥmad recorded it with the same meaning.
Ibn ʿAdī mentioned that this ʿAbd al-Wāḥid alone narrated it from ʿUrwah, and of this ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Bukhārī said: His hadith is munkar. Al-Ṭabarānī, however, recorded it: Hārūn ibn Kāmil told us,
Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam told us, Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd al-Madanī told us, Abū Ḥazrah Yaʿqūb ibn Mujāhid told me, ʿUrwah informed me, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned it.

This chain is sound, and all its narrators are reliable and have narrations recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ, except al-Ṭabarānī's shaykh, whose standing I cannot recall at present. Perhaps the narrator said, “Abū Ḥamzah told us,” meaning
ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Maymūn, and the listener imagined that he had said “Abū Ḥazrah”, and then supplied the full name himself on the strength of his mistake. And Allah knows best.

Al-Ṭabarānī and others recorded, through the narration of ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀtikah, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever humiliates an ally of Mine has come out openly to wage war on Me. Son of Ādam,

you will never attain what is with Me except by performing what I have made obligatory upon you. My servant keeps seeking My love through voluntary deeds until I love him, and then I am his heart with which he understands,

his tongue with which he speaks and his sight with which he sees. When he calls on Me, I answer him; when he asks of Me, I give to him; when he seeks My help, I help him. And the worship of My servant that I love most is sincere counsel (naṣīḥah).”
ʿUthmān and ʿAlī ibn Yazīd are both weak.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said of this hadith: It is extremely munkar.
It has also been narrated from the hadith of ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, with a weak chain; al-Ismāʿīlī recorded it in Musnad ʿAlī.

It has been narrated from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās with a weak chain. Al-Ṭabarānī recorded it, and its wording contains an addition. We have also narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās by another route, which is weak as well.

Al-Ṭabarānī and others recorded it from the hadith of al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā al-Khushanī, from Ṣadaqah ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Dimashqī, from Hishām al-Kinānī, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, from Jibrīl, from his Lord the Exalted, who said:

“Whoever humiliates an ally of Mine has come out openly to wage war on Me. I have not hesitated over anything I do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death and I dislike to cause him grief, yet he cannot escape it. Among My believing servants is one who wants a certain door of worship,

and I hold him back from it so that self-admiration does not enter him and corrupt him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything like the performance of what I have made obligatory upon him, and My servant keeps offering Me voluntary deeds until I love him. Whomever I love, I become for him hearing, sight, a hand and a supporter. He called on Me and I answered him;

he asked of Me and I gave to him; he was sincere towards Me and I was sincere towards him. Among My servants is one whose faith only wealth can set right; were I to make him poor, it would corrupt him. And among My servants is one whose faith only poverty can set right; were I to give him plenty, it would corrupt him.

Among My servants is one whose faith only health can set right; were I to make him ill, it would corrupt him. And among My servants is one whose faith only illness can set right; were I to make him healthy, it would corrupt him. I direct the affairs of My servants by My knowledge of what is in their hearts; I am All-Knowing, All-Aware.”
Al-Khushanī and Ṣadaqah are weak, and Hishām is unknown. Ibn Maʿīn was asked about this Hishām: Who is he?
He said: Nobody — meaning that he is not to be taken into account.
Al-Bazzār recorded part of the hadith by way of Ṣadaqah, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Anas.
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded from the hadith of al-Awzāʿī, from ʿAbdah ibn Abī Lubābah: Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh told me: I heard Ḥudhayfah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Allah the Exalted revealed to me: O brother of the messengers, O brother of the warners, warn your people not to enter any of My houses while anyone holds a claim against them for a wrong they have done him,
for I curse such a man as long as he stands before Me in prayer, until he returns that wrong to its owners. Then I will be his hearing with which he hears

and his sight with which he sees; he will be one of My allies and My chosen ones, and he will be My neighbour in Paradise with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs.” This chain is sound, but the hadith is very unusual (gharīb).
Let us return to explaining the hadith of Abū Hurayrah that al-Bukhārī recorded. It has been said to be the noblest hadith narrated on the subject of the allies of Allah (al-awliyāʾ).

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, “Whoever shows enmity to an ally of Mine, I have declared war on him,” mean: I have informed him that I am at war with him, since he is at war with Me by showing enmity to My allies.

That is why the hadith of ʿĀʾishah has, “has made it lawful to wage war on Me,” and the hadith of Abū Umāmah and others has, “has come out openly to wage war on Me.” Ibn Mājah recorded, with a weak chain, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal
that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “A little showing off is shirk, and whoever shows enmity to an ally of Allah has come out openly to wage war on Allah.

Allah the Exalted loves the righteous, the God-fearing, the hidden: those who are not missed when they are absent, and who, when present, are not invited and not recognised. Their hearts are lamps of guidance; they come safely out of every dark and murky [trial].”

The allies of Allah must be befriended, and showing enmity to them is unlawful, just as His enemies must be treated as enemies, and befriending them is unlawful. The Exalted says: “Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies” [al-Mumtaḥanah 60:1]. And He says:

“Your ally is only Allah, His Messenger and those who believe — those who establish the prayer and give zakāh while they bow down. And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and those who believe as allies — it is the party of Allah that will be victorious” [al-Māʾidah 5:55–56]. He also described those He loves, and who love Him, as humble towards the believers

and mighty against the disbelievers. Imam Aḥmad reported in Kitāb al-Zuhd, with his chain of narration, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā (peace be upon him) when He spoke to him:

Know that whoever humiliates an ally of Mine or frightens him has come out openly to wage war on Me, has opened hostilities with Me, and has exposed himself and called Me against himself. I am the swiftest of all to come to the aid of My allies. Does the one who wages war on Me think he can stand against Me?
Or does the one who vies with Me in might think he can thwart Me?
Or does the one who comes out openly against Me think he can outstrip Me or elude Me?
How could that be, when I am the One who avenges them in this world and the Hereafter? I do not entrust their support to anyone besides Myself.
Know that all acts of disobedience are a waging of war on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Al-Ḥasan said: Son of Ādam, have you any strength to wage war on Allah?

For whoever disobeys Allah has waged war on Him; but the uglier the sin, the fiercer the war against Allah. That is why Allah the Exalted called those who consume usury and highway robbers people who wage war on Allah the Exalted and His Messenger:

because of the enormity of their wrongdoing against His servants and their striving to spread corruption in His lands. The same is true of showing enmity to His allies, for the Exalted takes it upon Himself to support His allies; He loves them and strengthens them, so whoever shows enmity to them has shown enmity to Allah and waged war on Him. In a hadith, the Prophet ﷺ

said: “Allah, Allah, regarding my Companions! Do not make them a target. Whoever harms them has harmed me, whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever harms Allah, He will soon seize him.” Al-Tirmidhī and others recorded it.

His words: “My servant does not draw near to Me with anything like the performance of what I have made obligatory upon him, and My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him.” Having mentioned that showing enmity to His allies is waging war on Him, He went on to describe His allies, to whom it is unlawful to show enmity and whom it is obligatory to befriend,

by mentioning the means by which they draw near to Him. The root of walāyah (being an ally) is nearness, and the root of enmity is distance. The allies of Allah, then, are those who draw near to Him through what brings them close to Him, and His enemies are those whom He has distanced from Himself because of their deeds, which call for their being driven away and kept far from Him. He divided His allies who are brought near into two groups:
The first are those who draw near to Him by performing the obligations. This includes doing what is obligatory and leaving what is unlawful,
since all of that is among the obligations Allah has laid upon His servants.
The second are those who, after the obligations, draw near to Him through voluntary deeds. It is clear from this that there is no path leading to nearness to Allah the Exalted, to being His ally

and to His love, other than obedience to Him as He has laid it down on the tongue of His Messenger. Whoever claims to be an ally of Allah, to draw near to Him and to love Him by any other path is shown to be lying in his claim,

just as the idolaters sought nearness to Allah the Exalted by worshipping those they worshipped besides Him, as Allah tells of them that they said: “We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah” [al-Zumar 39:3];

and as He tells of the Jews and the Christians that they said: “We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones” [al-Māʾidah 5:18], while they persisted in denying His messengers, committing what He had forbidden and abandoning what He had made obligatory.
That is why He mentioned in this hadith that the allies of Allah are of two ranks.

The first are those who draw near to Him by performing the obligations. This is the rank of those who take the middle course (al-muqtaṣidūn), the people of the right. Performing the obligations is the best of deeds, as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

The best of deeds is performing what Allah has made obligatory, keeping scrupulously away from what Allah has made unlawful, and sincerity of intention in seeking what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said in his sermon: The best worship is performing the obligations and avoiding what is forbidden. That is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, laid these obligations on His servants only to bring them near to Him and to secure for them His good pleasure and His mercy.
The greatest of the bodily obligations that bring one near to Him is the prayer, as the Exalted says: “Prostrate and draw near” [al-ʿAlaq 96:19]. The Prophet ﷺ said:
“The nearest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating.” He also said: “When one of you is praying, he is conversing intimately with his Lord,” or “his Lord is between him and the qiblah.”
And he said: “Allah sets His Face towards the face of His servant in his prayer so long as he does not turn away.”

Among the obligations that bring one near to Allah the Exalted is a shepherd's justice towards his flock, whether the flock is general, as with a ruler, or particular, as with an ordinary person's justice towards his family and children, as he ﷺ said: “Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.”
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, the Prophet ﷺ said:

“The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light at the right hand of the Most Merciful — and both His hands are right hands — those who are just in their judgement, with their families and in whatever they are put in charge of.”
In al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Saʿīd, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The most beloved of servants to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and the nearest of them to Him in seating, is a just ruler.”

The second rank is that of the foremost, those brought near (al-sābiqūn al-muqarrabūn). They are those who, after the obligations, drew near to Allah by striving in voluntary acts of obedience and by holding back, out of scrupulousness, from the finer points of what is disliked. That brings about Allah's love for the servant, as He said:

“And My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him.” Whomever Allah loves, He grants love of Him, obedience to Him and occupation with His remembrance and His service; and that brings about for him nearness to Him, closeness in His presence and favour with Him, as Allah the Exalted says:

“Whoever of you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, who strive in the path of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills; and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing” [al-Māʾidah 5:54].

This verse indicates that if anyone turns away from Our love and turns his back on nearness to Us, We do not care; We replace him with one more fitting and more deserving of this gift than he is. Whoever turns away from Allah has no substitute for Allah, while Allah has substitutes for him.
I have no occupation but Him, no occupation at all; / no reproach can turn my heart from loving Him.
What am I to do if He turns away and hope is dashed? / There are substitutes for me, but for Him I have none.

In one of the old reports, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “Son of Ādam, seek Me and you will find Me. If you find Me, you have found everything; and if I escape you, everything has escaped you. And I am dearer to you than everything.”
Dhū al-Nūn used often to repeat these verses at night:
Seek for yourselves / the like of what I have found:
I have found a refuge / in whose love there is no toil.
If I go far away, He brings me near; / and if I draw near to Him, He comes close.

Whoever misses Allah would be the loser even if he gained the whole of Paradise; how much more so when he gains nothing but a small, paltry, contemptible share of an abode the whole of which is not worth a gnat's wing:
Whoever misses seeing You for a single day, / all his times are a loss;
and wherever I may be, in whatever land, / I turn towards Your Face.

Then He mentioned the qualities of those whom Allah loves and who love Him, saying: “humble towards the believers,” meaning that they treat the believers with humility, gentleness and a lowered wing; “mighty against the disbelievers,”

meaning that they treat the disbelievers with might, severity and harshness. Because they loved Allah, they loved His allies who love Him and treated them with love, tenderness and mercy; and they hated His enemies who show Him enmity and treated them with severity and harshness,

as the Exalted says: “severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves” [al-Fatḥ 48:29]. “They strive in the path of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer”: for part of perfect love is striving against the beloved's enemies. Moreover,

jihād in the path of Allah is a call to those who turn away from Allah to return to Him, by sword and spear, after they have been called to Him by argument and proof. The one who loves Allah loves to draw all creation to His door,
and whoever does not answer the call made with gentleness and kindness needs to be called with severity and force: “Your Lord marvels at a people who are led to Paradise in chains.”
“And they do not fear the blame of any blamer”:
the lover has no concern but what pleases his beloved, whoever is pleased and whoever is angered. Whoever fears blame for loving the one he loves is not truthful in his love:
Love has halted me where you are, and I have / no place to fall behind it and none to go ahead;
I find blame for loving you sweet, / for love of hearing you named; so let the blamers blame me.

His words, “That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills,” refer to the rank of those whom He loves and who love Him, with the qualities mentioned. “And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing”: vast in His giving, knowing who deserves His bounty, so that He grants it to him, and who does not deserve it, so that He withholds it from him.

It is reported that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) used to say: O Allah, make me one of those You love, for when You love a servant You forgive his sin even if it is great, and accept his deed even if it is small.

Dāwūd (peace be upon him) used to say in his supplication: O Allah, I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You and the love of the deeds that will bring me to Your love. O Allah, make love of You dearer to me than myself, my family and cool water.

The Prophet ﷺ said: “My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, came to me” — meaning in a dream — “and said to me: Muḥammad, say: O Allah, I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the deeds that will bring me to Your love.”

Among his supplications ﷺ was: “O Allah, grant me Your love and the love of those whose love will benefit me with You. O Allah, whatever You grant me of what I love, make it a strength for me in what You love. O Allah, whatever You keep from me of what I love, make it free time for me for what You love.”

It is narrated of him ﷺ that he used to supplicate: “O Allah, make love of You the dearest of all things to me and fear of You the most fearsome of all things to me; cut off from me the needs of this world through longing to meet You; and when You cool the eyes of the people of this world with their worldly goods, cool my eye with Your worship.”

The people of this rank among those brought near have no concern, then, except for what brings them near to the One who loves them and whom they love. One of the Salaf said: Deeds done out of fear may be altered by hope,

but deeds done out of love are never touched by slackness. Another of them said: When the idle grow weary of their idleness, those who love You will never grow weary of intimate converse with You and remembrance of You.
Farqad al-Sabakhī said: I read in one of the books: Whoever loves Allah holds nothing in higher preference than what He loves, and whoever loves this world

holds nothing in higher preference than his own desire. The one who loves Allah the Exalted is a commander placed over the commanders; his company will be the first of the companies on the Day of Resurrection, and his seat the nearest of seats there.

Love is the utmost of nearness and of striving. Those who love will never weary of long striving for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They love Him, love His remembrance and make Him beloved to His creation; they walk among His servants with sincere counsel,

and they fear for them because of their deeds on the day when disgraces are laid bare. They are the allies of Allah and His beloved ones, the people of His choosing; they are the ones who will have no rest short of meeting Him.
Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī said: The one who loves finds no pleasure in this world alongside love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and does not neglect the remembrance of Allah for the blink of an eye.
Muḥammad ibn al-Naḍr al-Ḥārithī said: One who loves Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, hardly ever tires of drawing near to Allah the Exalted, and hardly ever grows weary of it.

Another said: The one who loves Allah has a heart that soars and remembers Him much; he seeks His good pleasure by every way he can, through every means and voluntary deed, with persistence upon persistence and longing upon longing. One of them recited:
Love your Lord, that you may serve Him; / those who love are servants to the ones they love.
Another poet recited:
The lover wants nothing but his beloved's love; / the lover humbly offers every kind of goodness.
Among the greatest of the voluntary deeds by which a servant draws near to Allah the Exalted is reciting the Qurʾān often and listening to it with reflection, contemplation and understanding.
Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt said to a man: Draw near to Allah as much as you can, and know that you will never draw near to Him with anything dearer to Him than His own speech.

In al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Umāmah, as marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ): “Servants have not drawn near to Allah with anything like what came forth from Him,” meaning the Qurʾān. For those who love, nothing is sweeter than the speech of their beloved; it is the delight of their hearts and the goal of their seeking.
ʿUthmān said: If your hearts were pure, you would never have your fill of the speech of your Lord.
Ibn Masʿūd said: Whoever loves the Qurʾān loves Allah and His Messenger.
One of those who know Allah (al-ʿārifūn) asked a disciple: Have you memorised the Qurʾān?
He said: No. He said: Allah help us!
A disciple who has not memorised the Qurʾān! What does he take delight in? What does he chant?
With what does he converse intimately with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic?
One of them used to recite the Qurʾān a great deal, then became occupied with other things instead. He saw in a dream someone saying to him:
If you claim to love Me, / why have you shunned My Book?
Have you not reflected on what / it holds of My gentle reproach?
Among these deeds too is frequent remembrance of Allah in which heart and tongue agree.
In the Musnad of al-Bazzār, from Muʿādh, who said: I said: Messenger of Allah, tell me of the best of deeds and the nearest of them to Allah the Exalted.
He said: “That you die with your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.”

In the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs.”
And in another hadith: “I am with My servant so long as he remembers Me and his lips move in mentioning Me.”
And He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “So remember Me; I will remember you” [al-Baqarah 2:152].

When the Prophet ﷺ heard people raising their voices with takbīr and tahlīl while they were with him on a journey, he said to them: “You are not calling on one who is deaf or absent; you are calling on One who is All-Hearing and Near, and He is with you.”
In one narration: “He is nearer to you than the necks of your mounts.”

Among these too is loving the allies of Allah and His beloved ones for His sake, and showing enmity to His enemies for His sake. In the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet ﷺ

said: “Among the servants of Allah are people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, yet the prophets and the martyrs will envy them their station with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” They said: Messenger of Allah, who are they?
He said: “They are people who loved one another by the spirit of Allah, without any ties of kinship between them or wealth they exchanged. By Allah, their faces are light, and they are upon light.

They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve.” Then he recited this verse: “Truly, the allies of Allah — no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve” [Yūnus 10:62].

Something similar is narrated from the hadith of Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, from the Prophet ﷺ; in his hadith: “The prophets will envy them their nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and their seat with Him.”
In the Musnad, from ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The servant does not find pure faith until he loves for Allah's sake and hates for Allah's sake.

When he loves for Allah's sake and hates for Allah's sake, he has earned walāyah from Allah. My allies among My servants and My beloved ones among My creation are those who are remembered when I am remembered, and I am remembered when they are remembered.”
Al-Murtaʿish was asked: How is love attained?
He said: By befriending the allies of Allah and showing enmity to His enemies; and its root is conformity [to what He loves].
In al-Zuhd of Imam Aḥmad, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, who said: Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: My Lord, who are Your people, whom You shade in the shade of Your Throne?

He said: Mūsā, they are those whose hands are innocent and whose hearts are pure; who love one another for the sake of My majesty; who, when I am remembered, are remembered with Me, and when they are remembered, I am remembered with them; who perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly in times of hardship;

who turn back to My remembrance as eagles turn back to their nests; who cling to love of Me as a little child clings to people; and who become angry when what I have forbidden is made lawful, as a leopard becomes angry when it is provoked.

His words: “When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks.” In some narrations: “his heart with which he understands, and his tongue with which he speaks.”

What is meant by these words is that whoever strives to draw near to Allah through the obligations and then through voluntary deeds, He brings him near to Himself and raises him from the rank of faith to the rank of excellence (iḥsān), so that he comes to worship Allah with a sense of presence and watchfulness, as though he sees Him.

His heart is then filled with knowledge of Allah the Exalted, love of Him, awe of His greatness, fear of Him, reverence and veneration for Him, intimacy with Him and longing for Him, until this knowledge in his heart becomes something he witnesses with the eye of insight, as it has been said:
He dwells in the heart and fills it; / I do not forget Him, that I should then remember Him.
He is absent from my hearing and my sight, / but the core of my heart sees Him.
Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: Allah says: “Whoever claims to love Me and then sleeps away from Me has lied. Does not every lover love to be alone with his beloved?
Here I am, looking upon those who love Me: they have set Me before their eyes, addressed Me as one they behold, and spoken to Me in My presence. Tomorrow I will cool their eyes in My gardens.”

This that is in the hearts of those who love and are brought near keeps growing stronger until it fills their hearts, so that nothing else remains in them, and their limbs cannot move except in accord with what is in their hearts. Of one whose state is this,

it is said: Nothing remains in his heart but Allah — meaning knowledge of Him, love of Him and remembrance of Him. With this meaning is the well-known Israelite report: “Allah says: My heavens and My earth could not contain Me, but the heart of My believing servant contains Me.”
One of those who know Allah said: Beware of Him, for He is jealous and does not like to see anything else in His servant's heart. On this someone said:
There is no room for people in my heart: / love of you has grown in it until it is full.
Another poet said:
My heart was moulded to the measure of my love for them, / so there is no room in it for any love but theirs.

The Prophet ﷺ pointed to this meaning in his sermon when he came to Madīnah, saying: “Love Allah with all your hearts,” as Ibn Isḥāq mentioned in his Sīrah. When the heart is filled with the greatness of Allah the Exalted,

that erases from it everything besides Him, and nothing remains to the servant of his self and his desire, and no will except for what his Master wills from him. Then the servant speaks only in remembrance of Him

and moves only at His command. If he speaks, he speaks by Allah; if he hears, he hears by Him; if he looks, he looks by Him; and if he strikes, he strikes by Him. This is what is meant by His words: “I am his hearing with which he hears,

his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks.” Whoever points to anything other than this is pointing to the heresy of incarnation (ḥulūl) or of union (ittiḥād), of which Allah and His Messenger are free.
That is why some of the Salaf, such as Sulaymān al-Taymī, were regarded as not knowing how to disobey Allah.

A woman of the Salaf advised her children, saying: Make love of Allah and obedience to Him your habit, for the God-fearing grew so used to obedience that their limbs felt estranged from anything else. If the accursed one presents them with an act of disobedience, it passes them by abashed, and they disown it.

Of this meaning is ʿAlī's saying: We used to think that ʿUmar's devil was too much in awe of him to command him to sin. We indicated earlier that this is one of the special secrets of tawḥīd, for the meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh

is that none besides Him is taken as god in love, hope, fear and obedience. When the heart has realised complete tawḥīd, there remains in it no love for anything but what Allah loves, and no aversion to anything but what Allah dislikes; and whoever is like that, his limbs move only in obedience to Allah.

Sins arise only from loving what Allah dislikes or disliking what Allah loves, and that arises from putting the desire of the self before love and fear of Allah. That impairs the perfection of the obligatory tawḥīd, and because of it the servant falls into neglecting some obligations

or committing some prohibited things. But one whose heart has realised the tawḥīd of Allah has no concern left except for Allah and for what pleases Him. A hadith has come as marfūʿ: “Whoever wakes in the morning with his concern set on other than Allah is not of Allah.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded it from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb as mawqūf (his own words). He said: Whoever wakes in the morning with his greatest concern set on other than Allah is not of Allah.
One of those who know Allah said: If anyone tells you that an ally of His has any concern for anything but Him, do not believe him.

Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī used to call out at night: Concern for You has put an end to all my other concerns and bound me in a pact with sleeplessness; my longing to look upon You has tied pleasures fast away from me and stood between me and my appetites. So I am in Your prison, O Generous One, a wanted man. On this someone said:
They said: He has busied himself away from us and chosen another / in our place — and that is the act of a faithless, forgetful man.
But how could I turn my heart from loving you / to anything but remembering you, O you who are all my occupation?

His words: “If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks My refuge, I will surely grant him refuge.” In the other narration: “If he calls on Me, I answer him; and if he asks of Me, I give to him.” This means that this beloved one who is brought near has a special standing with Allah, such that when he asks Allah for something,

He gives it to him; when he seeks refuge with Him from something, He grants him refuge from it; and when he calls on Him, He answers him. So his supplications come to be answered because of his honour with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Many of the righteous Salaf were known for having their supplications answered.

In the Ṣaḥīḥ: al-Rubayyiʿ bint al-Naḍr broke a slave girl's front tooth. They offered her people compensation (arsh), and they refused; they asked them to forgive, and they refused. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged between them by retaliation. Anas ibn al-Naḍr said: Is al-Rubayyiʿ's tooth to be broken?

By the One who sent you with the truth, her tooth will not be broken! The people then agreed and took the compensation, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Among the servants of Allah are some who, if they swore by Allah, He would fulfil their oath.”

In al-Ḥākim's Ṣaḥīḥ, from Anas, the Prophet ﷺ said: “How many a weak man, looked down upon, in two worn-out garments, who, if he swore by Allah, He would fulfil his oath! Among them is al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik.” Al-Barāʾ met an advancing army of the idolaters, and the Muslims said to him:
Swear by your Lord. He said: I adjure You, my Lord, to give us their backs! And He gave them their backs. Then they met again, and they said:
Swear by your Lord. He said: I adjure You, my Lord, to give us their backs and to join me to Your Prophet ﷺ. They turned their backs in flight, and al-Barāʾ was killed.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā reported, with a chain of his, that al-Nuʿmān ibn Qawqal said on the day of Uḥud: O Allah, I adjure You that I be killed and enter Paradise. He was killed, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Al-Nuʿmān swore by Allah, and He fulfilled his oath.”
Abū Nuʿaym reported with his chain of narration from Saʿd that ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaḥsh said on the day of Uḥud: My Lord, when I meet the enemy tomorrow, bring me face to face with a man of fierce might,

fierce in his rage, whom I will fight for Your sake and who will fight me. Then let him take me and cut off my nose and my ears, so that when I meet You tomorrow You will say: ʿAbdullāh, who cut off your nose and your ears?

And I will say: [It was] for You and for Your Messenger. And You will say: You have spoken the truth. Saʿd said: I came upon him at the end of the day, and his nose and his ears were hanging on a thread.

Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ was one whose supplications were answered. A man told lies about him, and he said: O Allah, if he is lying, blind him, lengthen his life and expose him to trials. All of that befell the man. He used to accost slave girls in the streets, saying: An old man, put to trial — Saʿd's supplication struck me.
He supplicated against a man he heard reviling ʿAlī, and before the man had left his place a runaway camel came and trampled him with its forelegs and hind legs until it killed him.

A woman disputed with Saʿīd ibn Zayd over a piece of land of his, claiming that he had taken her land from her. He said: O Allah, if she is lying, blind her and kill her on her land. She went blind; and one night, as she was walking on her land, she fell into a well there and died.

Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī was on an expedition, and they grew thirsty. He prayed and said: O Allah, O All-Knowing, O Forbearing, O Most High, O Mighty, we are Your servants, and in Your path we fight Your enemy; so give us rain to drink from and make wuḍūʾ with,

and give no one but us a share in it. They went on a little and found a river of rainwater gushing; they drank and filled their vessels. Then they went on, and some of his companions went back to the place of the river and saw nothing, as though there had never been any water there at all.
Anas ibn Mālik was told that a piece of land of his in al-Baṣrah was suffering from drought. He made wuḍūʾ, went out into the open country and prayed two rakʿahs,
and supplicated. Rain came and watered his land, and it went hardly any further than his land.
Some reed huts burned down in al-Baṣrah in the time of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, and in the midst of them one hut was left unburnt. Abū Mūsā said to its owner: Why did your hut not burn?

He said: I adjured my Lord not to burn it. Abū Mūsā said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “In my nation there are men with dust-coloured heads and soiled clothes who, if they swore by Allah, He would fulfil their oath.”

Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī was famous for having his supplications answered. When a gazelle passed by him, the boys would say to him: Ask Allah to hold this gazelle for us. He would ask Allah, and He would hold it until they took it with their hands.

He supplicated that a woman who had spoiled his wife's companionship with him should lose her sight, and her sight went at once. She came to him and began imploring him by Allah and pleading with him; he had mercy on her and asked Allah, and He restored her sight, and his wife returned to her former state with him.
A man told lies about Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr. Muṭarrif said to him: If you are lying, may Allah hasten your death. The man died on the spot.

A man of the Khawārij used to attend the gathering of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and harm those present. When his harm grew worse, al-Ḥasan said: O Allah, You know how he harms us, so rid us of him however You will. The man fell down where he stood and was carried back to his family on his bier, dead.

Ṣilah ibn Ashyam was on an expedition when his mule went off with its load, and the people moved on. He stood up to pray and said: O Allah, I adjure You to return my mule and its load to me. It came and stood in front of him.

Once he was in a barren wilderness and grew hungry. He asked Allah for food and heard a thud behind him, and there was a cloth, or a kerchief, holding a basket of fresh ripe dates. He ate from it, and the cloth stayed with his wife Muʿādhah al-ʿAdawiyyah, who was one of the righteous women.

Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir was on a campaign when one of his companions said: I crave fresh cheese. Ibn al-Munkadir said: Ask Allah for food and He will feed you, for He is the One who is able. The people supplicated, and they had gone only a little way when they saw a basket sewn shut,

and it held fresh cheese. Some of the people said: If only it were honey! Ibn al-Munkadir said: The One who has fed you cheese here is able to feed you honey, so ask Him for it. They supplicated and went on a little, and found a vessel of honey on the road; they dismounted and ate.
Ḥabīb al-ʿAjamī Abū Muḥammad was known for having his supplications answered.

He supplicated for a boy whose head was bald, weeping as he did so and wiping the boy's head with his tears; before he rose, the hair of the boy's head had grown black, and he had some of the finest hair of anyone.
A crippled man was brought to him in a litter, and he supplicated for him. The man stood on his feet, carried his litter on his neck and went back to his family.

During a famine he bought a great deal of food and gave it in charity to the poor. Then he sewed some purses, put them under his bedding and supplicated to Allah. The owners of the food came to him asking for its price; he brought out those purses, and they were full of dirhams. He weighed them, and they came to exactly what was owed to them, so he handed them over.
A man used to mock him a great deal; Ḥabīb supplicated against him, and he was struck with leprosy.
Once he was with Mālik ibn Dīnār when a man came and spoke harshly to Mālik over some dirhams Mālik had distributed. When he had kept this up for a long time,
Ḥabīb raised his hand to the sky and said: O Allah, this man has distracted us from Your remembrance, so relieve us of him however You will. The man fell on his face, dead.

A group went out on a campaign in the path of Allah. One of them had a donkey, which died, and his companions moved on. He stood up, made wuḍūʾ and prayed, and said: O Allah, I came out striving in Your path and seeking Your good pleasure,

and I bear witness that You give life to the dead and raise those who are in the graves; so bring my donkey back to life for me. Then he went to the donkey and struck it, and the donkey stood up, shaking its ears. He rode it and caught up with his companions, and later he sold the donkey in al-Kūfah.

An expedition went out in the path of Allah and was struck by such severe cold that they nearly perished. They supplicated to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; beside them was a huge tree, and suddenly it was blazing with fire. They dried their clothes and warmed themselves by it until the sun rose on them; then they left, and the tree returned to its former state.

Abū Qilābah set out for Ḥajj while fasting, and went on ahead of his companions on a summer's day. He was struck by severe thirst and said: O Allah, You are able to take away my thirst without my breaking my fast.

A cloud shaded him and rained on him until it soaked his garment, and his thirst left him. He dismounted, dug out some pools and filled them; his companions reached him and drank, though none of that rain had fallen on them.
There is a great deal of this; it would take too long to record it all.
Most of the Salaf whose supplications were answered bore affliction patiently, choosing its reward, and did not ask relief from it for themselves.

It is narrated that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ used to supplicate for people, because they knew his supplications were answered. He was told: Why not ask Allah for your sight? — for he had gone blind. He said: Allah's decree is dearer to me than my sight.
One of them was afflicted with leprosy and was told: We have heard that you know Allah's greatest name; why not ask Him to remove what afflicts you?
He said: Son of my brother, it is He who afflicted me, and I would hate to oppose Him.
Ibrāhīm al-Taymī was told, while he was in al-Ḥajjāj's prison: Why not supplicate to Allah the Exalted? He said: I would hate to ask Him to relieve me of something in which I have a reward.
Likewise Saʿīd ibn Jubayr bore al-Ḥajjāj's harm patiently until al-Ḥajjāj killed him, though his supplications were answered.

He had a rooster that used to wake him at night for the prayer with its crowing. One night it did not crow at its usual time, and Saʿīd did not get up for the prayer. That distressed him, and he said: What is wrong with it?
May Allah cut off its voice! The rooster never crowed again after that, and his mother said to him: My son, do not supplicate against anything after this.

A man who had a high standing with Allah was mentioned to Rābiʿah; he lived on what he picked up from the things thrown away on rubbish heaps. A man said: What harm would it do this man to ask Allah to free him from needing this?
Rābiʿah said: When Allah decrees something for His allies, they are not displeased with it.
Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ lived in great hardship. He was told: Why not ask Allah to give you plenty? He took a pebble from the ground and said:
O Allah, make it gold — and it became a nugget of gold in his palm. Then he said: There is no good in this world except the Hereafter. And he said: He knows best what is good for His servants.

Sometimes a believer whose supplications are answered asks for something when Allah knows that what is best for him lies elsewhere; so He does not grant his request, and gives him in its place what is better for him, either in this world or in the Hereafter.

It has already been mentioned in the marfūʿ hadith of Anas: “Allah says: Among My servants is one who asks Me for a door of worship, and I hold him back from it so that self-admiration does not enter him.”
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded from the hadith of Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Thawbān, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Among my nation is one who, if he came to one of you asking for a dīnār, would not be given it;

if he asked him for a dirham, he would not be given it; and if he asked him for a copper coin, he would not be given it; yet if he asked Allah for Paradise, He would give it to him. He wears two worn-out garments and no one takes notice of him; if he swore by Allah, He would fulfil his oath.”
Others recorded it from the hadith of Sālim in mursal form, adding: “And if he asked Allah for something of this world, He would not give it to him, out of honour for him.”
His words: “I have not hesitated over anything I do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike to cause him grief.”

What is meant by this is that Allah the Exalted has decreed death for His servants, as the Exalted says: “Every soul shall taste death” [Āl ʿImrān 3:185]. Death is the parting of the soul from the body, and that comes about only with extremely great pain; it is the greatest of the pains that befall a servant in this world.

ʿUmar said to Kaʿb: Tell me about death. He said: Commander of the Faithful, it is like a tree with many thorns inside the son of Ādam, so that there is no vein or joint of his [that a thorn has not caught], and a man with powerful forearms is working at it, pulling it out. And ʿUmar wept.

When ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was dying, his son asked him to describe death. He said: By Allah, it is as though my sides were in a press, as though I were breathing through the eye of a needle, and as though a thorny branch were being dragged through me from my feet to the crown of my head.
A man at the point of death was asked: How do you find yourself?
He said: I find myself being dragged out, as if daggers were going back and forth inside me, and as if my insides were a heated oven blazing with fire.
Another was asked: How do you find yourself?
He said: I find it as though the heavens were closing down upon the earth with me between them, and I find my soul as though it were coming out through the eye of a needle.

Since death is this severe, and Allah the Exalted has made it inevitable for all His servants so that they cannot escape it, while He the Exalted dislikes the believer's being harmed and grieved, it was called hesitation in the case of the believer. As for the prophets (peace be upon them), they are not taken until they have been given the choice.

Al-Ḥasan said: Since the prophets disliked death, Allah made it easy for them by the meeting with Allah and by every gift or honour they loved, so that the soul of one of them is drawn out from between his sides while he loves it, because of what has been shown to him.
ʿĀʾishah said: After what I saw of the severity of the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I do not envy anyone whose death is made easy. She said: He had a cup of water beside him,

and he would put his hand into the cup, then wipe his face with the water and say: “O Allah, help me through the throes of death.” She said: And he began to say: “There is no god but Allah; truly, death has its throes.”
In a mursal hadith it is reported that he ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, You take the soul from among the sinews, the bones and the fingertips. O Allah, help me through death and make it easy for me.”

Some of the Salaf preferred to suffer hardship at death, as ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: I would not like the throes of death to be made easy for me; it is the last thing by which the believer's sins are expiated.
Al-Nakhaʿī said: They used to like to suffer hardship at death.
Some of them feared that a hard death might put them to trial. When Allah wills to make death easy for a servant, He makes it easy for him.

In the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Prophet ﷺ said: “When death comes to the believer, he is given the glad tidings of Allah's good pleasure and His honour, so that nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead of him; he loves to meet Allah, and Allah loves to meet him.”
Ibn Masʿūd said: “When the angel of death comes to take the soul of the believer, he says to him: Your Lord sends you greetings of peace.”

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: The angel of death says to him: Peace be upon you, ally of Allah; Allah sends you greetings of peace. Then he recited: “Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying: Peace be upon you” [al-Naḥl 16:32].

Zayd ibn Aslam said: The angels come to the believer when death is near and say to him: Do not fear what you are going to — and Allah takes away his fear — and do not grieve over this world and its people, and rejoice at the glad tidings of Paradise. So he dies with the glad tidings having come to him.

Al-Bazzār recorded from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah guards the death of His believing servant more jealously than any of you guards the choicest of his wealth, until He takes him on his bed.”
Zayd ibn Aslam said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has servants who are the people of well-being in this world and the Hereafter.”

Thābit al-Bunānī said: Allah has servants whom He guards jealously in this world from being killed and from pains. He lengthens their lives, makes their provision good, causes them to die on their beds and stamps them with the stamp of the martyrs.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and al-Ṭabarānī recorded it as marfūʿ by weak routes. In some of its wordings: “Allah has among His creation some whom He holds dear and keeps from affliction: He gives them life in well-being, causes them to die in well-being and admits them to Paradise in well-being.”
Ibn Masʿūd and others said: Sudden death is a relief for the believer.
Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī used to say: I hope that Allah will not choke me as I see you being choked at death. One night he was in his house, and they heard him call out:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān! — and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān had been killed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he went to the prayer place of his house and prayed, and he was taken while prostrating.
A number of the Salaf were taken in prayer while prostrating.
One of them used to say to his companions:
I will not die as you die; rather, I will be called and I will answer. One day, as he sat with his companions, he said, “Here I am (labbayk)!”, and then fell down dead.
One of them was sitting with his companions when they heard a voice saying: So-and-so, answer! By Allah, this is your last hour in this world. He leapt up and said: By Allah, this is death's herald.

He bade his companions farewell and greeted them with peace, then set off towards the voice, saying: Peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Then the voice ceased; they followed his tracks and found him dead.
One of them was sitting writing in a copy of the Qurʾān. He put the pen down and said: If this is how your death is, by Allah it is a good death. Then he fell down dead.
Another was sitting writing hadith. He put the pen down, raised his hands in supplication to Allah, and died.
